claim: In the named Danish official series, electric/hybrid vehicle fires per 10,000 are lower than the published rate for other vehicle types from 2018-2025
scope: BRS/ODIN/BIL54 definitions and denominator timing; observed fires, not age/mileage-adjusted causal risk
falsifier: BRS corrected series or matched age/exposure analysis reverses the comparison

claim: The simple public end-of-year Denmark stock is the denominator that generated the published 2024/2025 rates
scope: 50/485000 gives 1.031 not 1.2; 62/693000 gives 0.895 not 1.0; implied denominators are smaller
falsifier: BRS publishes the exact end-year denominator and calculation showing the difference is only rounding

claim: Sweden’s official 2024 electric/hybrid passenger-car arithmetic reproduces the published 0.45 per 10,000
scope: MSB/MCF incident summary, cars in traffic, no intentional fires; free-text search and near-miss/suspected-damage boundary
falsifier: official correction to the numerator or in-traffic stock

claim: Denmark, Sweden and Norway form one harmonized cross-country estimate
scope: Sweden/Norway may exclude fires spreading to buildings; years and source definitions differ
falsifier: harmonized shared case definition and same-year stock/exposure data

claim: Current Nordic lower per-vehicle rates prove lower lifetime or per-mile BEV ignition risk
scope: younger EV fleet, mileage, collision, charging and undercount are not jointly adjusted
falsifier: age/mileage-adjusted cohort or vehicle-year study with matched reporting

claim: EV fires have distinct consequence and suppression/toxic-gas concerns
locator: S4 pp.5-8; S6 official RISE summary
scope: separate outcome from ignition frequency; small experiments and incident descriptions
falsifier: larger same-model full-scale experiment showing no material difference in the named consequence endpoint

claim: NIST’s 5,718 estimate establishes EVs have higher risk than ICE vehicles
scope: multi-source EV/PHEV count with no matched ICE denominator and explicit undercount/identification assumptions
falsifier: matched denominator comparison from the same system
